sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)

contents.name: Qubit, Pauli matrices, and spin rotations
contents.reason: The chapter fixes a two-dimensional qubit basis and states the exact Pauli matrices and axis-rotation formula; the library fixes the ordered-register and first-linear conventions locally.

contents.name: The nine Pauli products, adjoints, and trace table
contents.reason: The source states Hermiticity, involution, anticommutation, and Pauli trace orthogonality; all nine products and signs are computed locally from the displayed matrices.

contents.name: Bloch coordinate representation and positivity ball
contents.reason: §2.3.2 supplies the Bloch expansion and formulas; its determinant/eigenvalue argument is reconstructed completely from two-by-two entries and local Pauli identities.

contents.name: Purity and the boundary sphere
contents.reason: The source identifies the unit-radius boundary with pure states; the local proof supplies the trace-square identity and the rank-one equivalence under the repository's density definition.

contents.name: Axis rotations and their exponential formula
contents.reason: §2.2.1, Eqs. (2.29)–(2.31), gives the Pauli matrices, square identity, and half-angle formula; the complete convergent-series and unitarity proof is supplied locally.

contents.name: Hadamard matrix and |0>, H|0> calculations
contents.reason: The cited chapter sections do not supply the Hadamard conjugation identities; these are proved by explicit local matrix multiplication.

sources.reading_verification: This turn inspected the complete cited passages in the locally retained full chapter extraction: §2.2.1, PDF pp.10–11, and §2.3.2, PDF pp.21–22. The retained qc_r2 source ledger reports the official 53-page chapter was read sequentially in full by its assigned researcher; this batch does not claim that prior reading as its own. The chapter uses the source bra/ket convention, while all authored formulas are translated to the root linear-first matrix convention. Physical postulates are not proof premises.

sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6 (2026-08-27)
sources.locator: §1.3, PDF pp.7–8; §1.4, PDF p.9; Appendix A.9, PDF p.198.

contents.name: Single-qubit space and ordered basis states
contents.reason: §1.3 describes a qubit as C² with the two computational basis vectors; the local definition states the ordered basis and density/ray interfaces precisely.

contents.name: Pauli matrices, Hermiticity, unitarity, and anticommutation
contents.reason: Appendix A.9 independently records the Pauli matrices, Hermiticity, involution, anticommutation, and trace orthogonality; the complete nine-product table is calculated locally.

contents.name: Exact H, X, Z, phase and T gates
contents.reason: §1.4 provides the exact matrices and phase-gate conventions; local verification proves unitarity and preserves the scalar phases.

contents.name: Hadamard action and the |0>, |+> basis check
contents.reason: §1.4 displays H and its action on the computational basis; all three Pauli conjugations, especially the Y sign, are proved locally.

contents.name: Bloch expansion from the Pauli basis
contents.reason: Appendix A.9 gives an independent Hermitian-Pauli-basis treatment; trace-one normalization and all coordinate identities are proved locally.

sources.reading_verification: This turn inspected the complete cited passages in the retained 239-page full-text extraction: §1.3, §1.4, and Appendix A.9. The qc_r1 source ledger reports a complete sequential read of the 239-page notes; this batch does not claim that prior reading as its own. The source uses a linear-second inner product, and the local item dependencies retain the root linear-first convention.

sources.title: Aram Harrow, 6.443/8.371/18.436 Quantum Information Science II, Lecture 1: Quantum states and operations (2018)

short_document_reading.publication: Aram Harrow, 6.443/8.371/18.436 Quantum Information Science II, Lecture 1: Quantum states and operations, February 7, 2018
short_document_reading.completeness_evidence: The official MIT PDF has exactly 3 pages by mutool page-tree inspection; this turn extracted and inspected every page and compared the Bloch-ball passage against the complete web PDF view.

contents.name: Density matrix conventions and qubit state set
contents.reason: The lecture states the trace-one positive semidefinite density-matrix interface; the active definitions make the nonzero space and root inner-product hypotheses explicit.

contents.name: Hermitian Pauli basis and Bloch-ball coordinates
contents.reason: §1.2.1 gives the Pauli-basis expansion and trace normalization; the complete finite-coordinate proof is local.

contents.name: Eigenvalue criterion for the closed unit ball
contents.reason: Eq. (1.3) states the radius bound but directs the reader to justify the Pauli-sum eigenvalues; the local proof supplies that omitted calculation, including r=0 and the unit-radius endpoint.

contents.name: Pure states lie on the sphere
contents.reason: The lecture states the boundary characterization; the local proof derives the trace-square identity and rank-one criterion.

contents.name: The |0> and |+> coordinate examples
contents.reason: §1.2.1 identifies |0> with the positive z-axis and |0>±|1> with the x-axis; the local example calculates all Pauli traces and proves H|0>=|+>.

sources.reading_verification: This turn downloaded the 211,213-byte official PDF, verified its 3-page count with mutool, extracted the complete text of PDF pp.1–3, and inspected all three pages. The lecture leaves the Pauli-sum eigenvalue computation as an exercise; it is not used as a proof supplier for that step.
